maria_cs: Ignite onboarding - seeing intermittent 401s then 429s when running the python SDK warmup. Customer says their init job fails 3/10 times. @kevin_dev can you take a look?
ignite-infra: we spin up ~30 worker processes at start, each does an auth handshake then a small generate. getting 401 then a few seconds later 429s. happening in our staging CI mostly.
kevin_dev: which SDK/version and how are you instantiating the client?
ignite-infra: python redwood-sdk v0.9.2 via pip. snippet: from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key='REDACTED')
then each worker calls client.generate concurrently.
maria_cs: ok, can you paste a sanitized sequence of the HTTP responses showing headers like x-rate-limit and retry-after?
ignite-infra: pasted logs: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
retry-after: 3
x-request-id: ignite-xyz-42
kevin_dev: thanks. two likely contributors: 1) when many processes hit our auth service at once it can return transient 401s due to a cold cache/DB hot path, and 2) the parallel init creates a stampede that exhausts the account-level init quota so you see 429s. quick mitigations: reuse a single auth client per host (share token), reduce init concurrency, and add exponential backoff with jitter on 401/429.
sanjeev_sre: also confirm their rate plan - the free onboarding tier has a soft limit on initiation handshakes (roughly 60/min). 30 workers doing multiple handshakes per deploy will exceed that easily. We can temporarily relax it for onboarding.
kevin_dev: small repro change you can try immediately: set env REDWOOD_CLIENT_PARALLEL=4 or construct client with Client(init_concurrency=4). Also enable a client-side header so we can trace: client.set_header('X-Client-Trace','ignite-warmup') and paste resulting logs. Example backoff pseudocode:
```python
# naive single-token cache to avoid stampede
from threading import Lock
_token = None
_lock = Lock()
def get_token():
    global _token
    with _lock:
        if _token and not expiring_soon(_token):
            return _token
        _token = fetch_new_token()
        return _token
```
This avoids each worker doing a separate token exchange.
ignite-infra: tried the single-token approach on one host and saw much fewer 401s. but they still saw occasional 401 even when token cached for 30s.
maria_cs: that could be clock skew across their containers vs our auth TTL enforcement. ask them to check NTP sync. Also we can offer a temporary token TTL bump while they ramp. @sanjeev_sre can we grant a short TTL extension for the account?
sanjeev_sre: yes we can apply a one-off TTL bump to 120s for ignite-1234 for 24h; filing internal ticket now and will post the ticket id here. Meanwhile please apply the init_concurrency change and backoff.
ignite-infra: applying init_concurrency=4 + jittered backoff now. will run a 20-run warmup. will report back in 15m.
kevin_dev: if you still see 401s after this change, enable header tracing and include x-request-id, x-rate-limit-remaining, and retry-after values. we'll also correlate with our auth logs.
ignite-infra: update - after the change warmups look stable, only 1 flaky run out of 30. thanks. can we schedule a short pairing to add the single-token pattern to their deploy template?
maria_cs: yes - booking 30m. proposed: tomorrow 14:00 PST. Invitees: @kevin_dev, @sanjeev_sre, @ignite-infra. Action items: 1) kevin_dev to add a short snippet to onboarding docs showing init_concurrency and single-token cache, 2) sanjeev_sre to apply TTL bump and follow up with ticket id, 3) ignite-infra to confirm no 401/429s over next 24h. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: doc PR created - PR #789 - docs/onboarding/python-init-concurrency.md
kevin_dev: I'll draft the snippet and ping for review.
ignite-infra: thanks everyone, will report back after the next deploy.
